_source: Headless /modernize run on the wordpress sample (internal validation pipeline, 2026-10-03; deliverables/wordpress/report.json + llm_response.json). The run did not retain assignment/v2/assignment.json, so engine_tables is RECONSTRUCTED from report.json: each engine's schema design is built only from its in-scope queries (filter_collector_for_assignment), so the tables its design covers (table_mappings primary + alternatives) and the tables touched by the queries linked to its in-scope access patterns are in that engine's assignment scope. recommended_engine lists [source_table, table_mappings[].recommended_database] pairs (secondary info only). llm_executive_summary is the summary the rubric judge flagged (#205), verbatim.
llm_executive_summary: The WordPress workload moves to a hybrid architecture with a cache tier: DynamoDB serves the majority of queries, including option, post, post meta and term lookups, while ElastiCache handles the high-frequency leaderboard and cached reads. Aurora MySQL keeps the multi-table joins with aggregation and the text search queries that DynamoDB and ElastiCache cannot serve, which removes the need for a separate OpenSearch Service deployment. Each engine takes the queries it fits best, so key-value reads scale without row-locking contention on the relational store. The migration leaves Aurora MySQL with a small, well-defined set of relational queries and gives the hot read paths single-digit millisecond access.
